lines.meet: I'm Taras, and this is Kashtan. Stay on the path, please, and don't touch anything that glows.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're near Ariden's Watch too, by the look of your boots. I'm at the gate by the wash troughs, Taras, and Kashtan.
lines.ask_home: Which city did you start out in? Kashtan wants to know, he's very nosy.
lines.ask_work: What was the job, before? Something with fewer ghosts than mine, I hope.
lines.answer_home: Kyiv, on the left bank. My mother grew more tomatoes on one balcony than any balcony should hold.
lines.answer_work: Tour guide in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, nine years. A minibus that smelled of instant coffee, and every tour ended under the Ferris wheel.
lines.chat_food: Varenyky with potato and a lot of sour cream, and salo on black bread. Kashtan prefers the salo.
lines.chat_sleep: Kashtan sleeps across my feet and snores, and I've stopped minding. I sleep well enough.
lines.chat_missing: The checkpoint at dawn, frost on the barrier, and every stray dog in the Zone waiting for my pockets.
lines.chat_here: Kashtan came through with me, and that's the luckiest thing that's happened to me. I'm not alone, at least.
lines.tease_quiet: Zone tourists like you were my favourites, {name}. Quiet, and you never touched anything.
lines.tease_talker: My tourists talked like you, {name}, right up until the Geiger counter started clicking.
lines.tease_careful: You count heads as much as I do, {name}, and Kashtan approves.
lines.tease_bold: You'd lick the Elephant's Foot if somebody dared you, {name}, and I'd have to explain it to your mother.
lines.tease_any: Kashtan likes you, {name}, and he's a very poor judge of character. I'm still deciding.
lines.tease_back: Ha, dry enough for the Zone, {name}. You've impressed me.
lines.bristle: Not about that, {name}, please. Some things aren't for jokes.
lines.apologise: That was cruel, and I'm sorry. Kashtan is ashamed of me, look at him.
lines.double_down: I'll say it twice if I must. Somebody should, before it costs you something.
lines.needle_quiet: You saw that and didn't say. Invisible things are the ones that kill you, so please say.
lines.needle_talker: Please, quiet for a minute. The ground's trying to tell me something, and you're drowning it out.
lines.needle_careful: Careful is good, I'm careful, but you've stopped moving altogether.
lines.needle_bold: You touch everything. Every tourist who touched things, I had to scrub down at the checkpoint.
lines.needle_any: You're not afraid of what you can't see. That's exactly what worries me about you.
lines.bite_back: I've walked this party out of worse places than this, counting heads the whole way. Remember that before you call me careless.
lines.hurt: Okay, that stung. Kashtan and I need a walk.
lines.laugh_off: Tourists called me worse when I wouldn't let them climb the Ferris wheel. It's fine, I'm used to it.
lines.confide: {name}, my father was a liquidator in 1986, and the cleanup killed him slowly when I was a teenager. I became a guide partly to understand it.
lines.listen: Kashtan's lying on your foot, {name}, so you may as well talk. I'm right here with you.
lines.look_out: Stay on the path in there, {name}, and don't touch anything that glows.
lines.accept: Okay, {name}, I trust you on this one.
lines.deflect: I'm fine, {name}, Kashtan's already checked. He's very thorough.
lines.check_in: Stop, {name}, let me count. Arms, legs, all still there?
lines.blame: Somebody stepped off the path in there. I asked very clearly.
lines.thank: Dyakuyu, thank you. Kashtan says you get sausage for life now.
lines.brush_off: It was nothing, I count heads both ways. You were on the list.
lines.worry: Kashtan was howling, {name}, and he never howls. Sit down, let me look.
lines.handed_down: So I'm carrying your gear now. Kashtan's already sniffed it, so it's officially ours.
lines.hand_fine: It's yours now, and it fits you. Kashtan's all the equipment I really need.
lines.hand_sulk: Kashtan noticed before I did, and he's not happy. Next time, ask.
lines.turn_friendly: You're on my head count now, {name}, every trip, going out and coming back.
lines.turn_friends: Kashtan would follow you out of the Zone, {name}, and so would I.
lines.turn_grating: We don't walk well together, I think. I'm still counting you, though.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still count you out and count you back. That's the job, liking you isn't.
lines.make_up: Enough of this, {name}. Kashtan's sulking, and he never sulks.
lines.defend: No, I was watching the whole time, and that's wrong. Let {name} be.
lines.friend_left: My head count's one short while {name}'s away. I keep recounting, out of habit.
lines.friend_back: Head count's right again, {name}'s back. Kashtan's beside himself.
lines.common_radiation: You've lived near the invisible kind of danger, haven't you? People who have never stop listening for the click.
lines.common_animals: Every dog at every checkpoint in the Zone knew my pockets. People who love animals can always find each other.
lines.common_ukrainian: Someone from home, slava Bohu. Which city, and do you miss the bread as much as I do?
